name: Orchestration & Tooling
oneLiner: The glue around a model call: prompts, retrieval, tools, frameworks, evaluation and guardrails.

analogy.text: A film crew around an actor: scripts, props and cues so the performance fits the scene.
analogy.breaks: An actor improvises from real understanding of the set. A model only sees what is placed in its context window: if the crew forgets a prop, for the model it doesn't exist.

examples: Guardrail and eval tools (e.g. Llama Guard, promptfoo)
givesAbove: Reliable, grounded model calls that can use your data and tools.
needsBelow: An inference endpoint from Inference & Optimization.

walkthrough.title: A question arrives
walkthrough.text: Someone asks their home-lab assistant: “Which driver did I install on the GPU box last month?” The model alone can't know.

walkthrough.title: Memory and retrieval look it up
walkthrough.text: Memory recalls a saved note about the GPU box, and retrieval searches the setup docs for driver notes. Both hand back short passages.

walkthrough.title: A tool checks the live machine
walkthrough.text: The model asks for a tool call to read the installed driver version. The application runs it and the result joins the context.

walkthrough.title: The context is packed and the model answers
walkthrough.text: System prompt, tool list, notes, the tool result and the question are trimmed to fit the window, stable parts first so they can be cached.

walkthrough.title: Guardrails check, evals keep score
walkthrough.text: Tool output is screened for injected orders, the answer is checked before it is shown, and the same question joins an eval set for the next change.
